2024-08-05 · Paper · Communications Biology 7, 946

Critical dynamics in spontaneous EEG predict anesthetic-induced loss of consciousness and perturbational complexity

Maschke C, O'Byrne J, Colombo MA, Boly M, Gosseries O, Laureys S, Rosanova M, Jerbi K, Blain-Moraes S

In 15 healthy adults under three anaesthetics, resting EEG predicted the stimulation-based consciousness index closely.

Volunteers were put under with propofol, xenon or ketamine; all stopped responding, but only the ketamine group reported vivid dreams afterwards. Measures of how close the resting brain sits to a 'critical' tipping point separated the dreaming group from the others, and predicted each person's score on the magnetic-pulse test.

15 healthy adults (propofol 5, xenon 5, ketamine 5), data from earlier studies. Avalanche criticality, chaoticity and related metrics; unconsciousness moved away from criticality and the edge of chaos. Ridge regression on 16 features predicted PCImax; leave-one-subject-out (15 folds) mean absolute error 0.065 (+/- 0.042); a 0.35 threshold separated conscious and unconscious states for true and predicted PCImax.

What we do with it

If true, the best-validated measure could be tested on many more open datasets. Caution: 15 subjects, 5 per drug, and the same cohort as Colombo 2019 and Sarasso 2015, so these are not independent replications. We test it out of sample. Planned
